blocks.text: Imagine a busy highway where cars must merge into a single lane without colliding. Medium Access Control (MAC) protocols aim to solve a similar problem in computer networks: how multiple devices can share a communication channel efficiently and fairly.

blocks.markdown: Medium Access Control (MAC) protocols are essential for managing how data packets are transmitted over a shared communication medium. They ensure that data is sent and received efficiently, minimizing collisions and maximizing throughput.

blocks.title: CSMA/CD
blocks.text: Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD) is a protocol used in wired networks to detect and manage collisions during data transmission.

blocks.markdown: In CSMA/CD, a device listens to the channel before transmitting. If the channel is clear, it sends data. If a collision is detected, the device stops transmitting, waits for a random time, and tries again.

blocks.caption: Time to detect a collision, where $d$ is the distance between the two farthest nodes and $c$ is the speed of signal propagation.

blocks.title: Collision Detection in CSMA/CD
blocks.prompt: Calculate the collision detection time for a network where the farthest nodes are 1000 meters apart and the signal propagation speed is $2 \times 10^8$ m/s.

steps.text: Identify the given values: $d = 1000$ meters, $c = 2 \times 10^8$ m/s.
Use the formula for collision detection time: $T_{coll} = \frac{2 \times d}{c}$.

blocks.answer: The collision detection time is $10^{-5}$ seconds.

blocks.title: CSMA/CA
blocks.text: Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance (CSMA/CA) is used in wireless networks to prevent collisions by using techniques like acknowledgments and time slots.

blocks.markdown: Wireless networks use CSMA/CA because detecting collisions is challenging due to the hidden node problem. Instead, they focus on avoiding collisions by reserving the channel before sending data.

blocks.title: Throughput Calculation with Collisions
blocks.prompt: Consider a network with a data rate of 10 Mbps and a collision probability of 0.1. Calculate the effective throughput.

steps.text: Identify the given values: data rate = 10 Mbps, collision probability = 0.1.
Calculate the effective throughput: $\text{Throughput} = \text{Data Rate} \times (1 - \text{Collision Probability})$.

points: CSMA/CD detects collisions and uses random backoff to recover.
CSMA/CA avoids collisions using acknowledgments and time slots.
Effective throughput is reduced by the probability of collisions.
